title: Billie Eilish im Star-Porträt: Liebesgerüchte Nat Wolff, Freund, Vermögen, Tour
content: Billie Eilish, a 24-year-old singer-songwriter, has become one of the most influential figures in the music industry. Born as Eilish Pirate Baird O'Connell, she rose to fame with her debut album 'When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?' in 2019, which earned her three Grammy Awards. She has since released two more successful albums, 'Happier Than Ever' (2021) and 'Hit Me Hard and Soft' (2024), both written with her brother Finneas O'Connell. Eilish's music is characterized by deep, often dark lyrics and innovative sound. She has been open about her struggles with depression and has used her platform to raise awareness about mental health. Eilish has also been vocal about her bisexuality and has criticized the media for outing her. She has been in relationships with several people, including rapper Brandon Adams and actor Jesse Rutherford, and has been spotted with actor Nat Wolff. Eilish's net worth is estimated to be around $53 million, and she has been named one of the most successful musicians in the world. She has also been recognized for her activism, including her support for the environment and her criticism of the music industry's treatment of artists.

title: Billie Eilish Soars Back To No. 1 On Multiple Charts
content: Billie Eilish’s second studio album, 'Hit Me Hard and Soft', re‑released as a collector’s‑edition vinyl in May 2024, has surged on Billboard charts. The album is now No. 1 on both the Top Rock & Alternative Albums and Top Alternative Albums charts, marking its 45th week at the top of the former and its 10th week atop the latter, and is one week shy of tying her debut album for longest‑running No. 1. It re‑entered the Vinyl Albums chart at No. 2 and climbed to No. 2 on the Top Album Sales chart, up from No. 48 on the 50‑spot list the previous week. On the Billboard 200 it moved from No. 24 to No. 6, while the Top Streaming Albums chart saw it rise from No. 21 to No. 18, driven by anniversary buzz rather than vinyl sales. The album’s performance underscores the impact of the re‑issue and the sustained popularity of Eilish’s music.

title: When is Spotify Wrapped 2025 out?
content: Spotify Wrapped 2025 is expected to be released in early December 2025, following a pattern from previous years—2024 was released on December 4, 2023 on November 30, 2022 on November 30, 2021 on December 1, and 2020 on December 1. The feature compiles users’ personalized listening data, including top songs, artists, genres, and total listening time, and presents it with dynamic graphics for social sharing. In 2024, Taylor Swift was named the Global and UK top artist for the second consecutive year, with over 26.6 billion streams attributed to her Grammy-nominated album 'The Tortured Poets Department'. Sabrina Carpenter topped the global songs chart with 'Espresso', and all five of the most-streamed albums of 2024 were by women: Swift, Billie Eilish ('Hit Me Hard and Soft'), Sabrina Carpenter, Karol G ('Mañana Será Bonito'), and Ariana Grande ('Eternal Sunshine'). Spotify has not confirmed the exact release date for 2025, but users are advised to ensure their app is updated to receive the data. The tracking period remains ambiguous—Spotify previously stated it ended in October 2021, but in 2023 confirmed it continued past October 31. Users can access their Wrapped data via the Spotify app once it becomes available.

title: Khalid: After the Sun Goes Down review - The soul of bedroom pop, the ache of Billie Eilish
content: Khalid, the 27-year-old Texan singer known for his low-key presence despite 50 million monthly Spotify streams, released his fourth album, 'After the Sun Goes Down,' in October 2025. The album, described as gorgeously gauzy and introspective, reflects a newfound sense of freedom following his public coming out on TikTok in late 2024, which he initially called 'nasty' but later embraced as a 'new spark of creativity.' The 17-track record blends bedroom pop sensibilities with soulful, introspective R&B, evoking artists like Billie Eilish, Clairo, and the early Weeknd. Lyrically, it explores themes of love, self-acceptance, and the emotional toll of living in the closet, as heard in songs like 'In Plain Sight' and 'Nobody (Make Me Feel).' Musically, it ranges from jazz-infused opener 'Medicine' to the sitar-driven 'Out of Body' and the Auto-Tune-heavy 'Tank Top' featuring Tove Lo. The album uses metaphors of travel—Cadillacs, Lexuses, and autobahns—to symbolize liberation and connection. Despite its dreamy, meandering pace, the record maintains emotional depth and concludes with a brooding, electro ballad that echoes Billie Eilish’s dark aesthetic. According to The Irish Times, the album is a 'grippingly untethered' yet 'firmly centered' expression of love, freedom, and self-acceptance.

title: Billie Eilish Misses Returning To No. 1 By One Space
content: Billie Eilish’s third full‑length album, *Hit Me Hard and Soft*, has re‑entered the Official Vinyl Albums chart at No. 2 after a brief absence, narrowly missing a return to the top spot.  The album has now spent 51 weeks on the chart, with 17 weeks inside the top 10, and this week marks its first top‑10 appearance since February.  While it remains at No. 20 on the Official Album Streaming chart, it has climbed to No. 6 on both the Official Album Sales and Official Physical Albums charts, and jumped from No. 25 to No. 10 on the overall Official Albums list.  Eilish’s other albums also appear on the vinyl chart: *When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?* is absent, *Happier Than Ever* moved from No. 31 to No. 28, and the album has slipped on four other lists simultaneously.  These movements demonstrate the sustained commercial impact of the anniversary vinyl release, which sold well enough to almost reconquer the UK chart.  The data show that the album’s performance is largely driven by vinyl sales, with streaming numbers remaining steady.

title: Taylor Swift rompe el récord de Spotify con 'The Fate of Ophelia' y destrona a Miley Cyrus
content: Taylor Swift broke Spotify's record with 'The Fate of Ophelia,' amassing over 101.8 million streams in its first seven days, surpassing the previous records set by her own 'Flowers' and BTS's 'Butter,' which had 99.3 million streams in its debut week. The song also broke the record for most streams in a single day, exceeding the 25 million streams achieved by her earlier track 'Fortnight' in April 2024, which had displaced Adele’s 'Easy on Me' as the top-streamed song in a day. 'The Fate of Ophelia' is part of the album 'The Life of a Showgirl,' which launched on October 3, 2025, and became the most-streamed album in a single day on Spotify within 12 hours and reached over five million pre-saves—both new platform records. Swift promoted the album with live performances on major late-night shows including The Graham Norton Show, The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, and Late Night With Seth Meyers. Industry sources predict all 12 tracks from the album will debut in the top 12 of the Billboard Hot 100, a feat only previously achieved by Swift and Drake. The album, described by critics as 'the most cinematic portrait' of her career, blends jazz, orchestral pop, and autobiographical lyrics, marking a new, more theatrical creative phase. The success of 'The Life of a Showgirl' reinforces Swift’s dominant influence over global streaming, with each release now serving as a cultural event, elevating not only her legacy but the benchmark for digital success in the music industry.

title: Billie Eilish: cómo transformó la depresión y ansiedad en arte que sana...
content: Billie Eilish has transformed her struggles with depression and anxiety into therapeutic art, as highlighted in a feature from cosmopolitan.com.mx published on October 14, 2025. The article details how Eilish, through her music and public vulnerability, redefined feminine strength by embracing imperfection and emotional honesty. Her collaboration with her brother, Finneas O’Connell, played a crucial role during a dark period when she experienced suicidal thoughts. Finneas initially declined to help with the song 'Everything I Wanted' out of concern for exacerbating her pain, but later returned when she was in a more stable mental state, turning the track into a mutual declaration of support. The article emphasizes that Eilish’s art serves as both personal healing and a source of comfort for others. Her oversized style, soft voice, and candid lyrics, combined with her advocacy for mental health—such as disconnecting without guilt and using art as refuge—have made her a symbol of emotional authenticity. The piece also notes that both Billie and Finneas come from an artistic family, with their mother, Maggie Baird, being an actress and musician, and their father, Patrick O’Connell, involved in entertainment. Finneas has produced and co-written all of Billie’s albums and prioritizes their creative and emotional bond as essential to their work. The article concludes with the message that while mental health is not cured overnight, it can be transformed—and when pain is turned into art, healing extends beyond the individual.
